title: Engine Card Layout Lab
summary: Studies the shipped engine card's internal layout. BASE is traced from EnginesScreen.kt and reproduces three real defects: (1) nothing is top-aligned (row is CenterVertically + spec column Arrangement.Center, so name and SPEED drift apart on tall cards), (2) the languages value is indented 4dp by EngineLanguagesValue's padding(horizontal = 4.dp), breaking the spec column's left edge, (3) both buttons bunch right via Arrangement.End. Variants: C1 the fix (no rule, top-aligned, flush languages, Uninstall left), C2 +roomier gap, C3 +faint panel behind specs, C4 +one-line label/value specs, C5 stacked (specs as a full-width row under full-width text). Plus an action-row study A1 both-right / A2 split / A3 both-left. Kitten/Kokoro/Pocket each, light + dark, 400dp, shipped 4-tick traffic-light meter.
decision: OPEN — awaiting Max. Lab leans C1 + A2 (split: Uninstall left, primary right). C5 (stacked) flagged as the one genuinely different idea — full-width description. First lab revision got BASE wrong (drew it top-aligned); retraced from source after Max caught it on device.

title: Engines Local/Cloud Split Lab
summary: Should the Engines tab separate on-device engines from cloud voices with a switch? Today it's one scroll (3 local A3 cards + the Cloud voices card last). 4 directions: T1 segmented control at top (On-device | Cloud, Toast-selected not accent), T2 Material TabRow at top, T3 segmented control pinned at bottom for thumb reach, T4 no-tab labelled sections (ON-DEVICE / CLOUD overlines) as the low-cost counter-option. Framed around the real boundary: on-device sends nothing, cloud transmits your text to a provider. Shows the shipped A3 card with the new traffic-light speed meter. Light + dark, 400dp.
decision: T1 (segmented switch, top) IMPLEMENTED in EnginesScreen.kt — On-device / Cloud pill, NO count badges (Max's call), selected segment = primaryContainer Toast not accent, selectable role=Tab, saveable state; list splits local engines vs the single Cloud card. Strings engines_tab_local/engines_tab_cloud across all 8 locales. Pending Max's on-device sign-off. Cloud-side privacy note deliberately omitted (extra copy + translations; consent gate already covers it).

title: Choose Engines Lab
summary: Rework the onboarding engine picker away from a wall of prose. 4 directions (A1 compact rows, A2 speed gauge, A3 spec columns, A4 hero badge), each leading with a speed signal then compact quality + language chips, size as a small number, license behind show-more. Recommends Kitten Nano (flips from Kokoro). Light + dark, 400dp.
decision: A3 spec columns shipped (commit f9aca5b). Two refinements of the shipped A3 card are now studied in their own labs: recommended-badge-lab and languages-affordance-lab.

title: Recommended Badge Lab
summary: Fix + reposition the 'Recommended' badge on the shipped A3 engine card. On device the inline pill (placed in a Row after the engine name) is starved of width by the long 'Kitten Nano (v0.8)' name and char-wraps into a vertical letter strip. 5 placements: R1 own line, R2 eyebrow/kicker, R3 corner tab, R4 full-width header strip, R5 inline name-priority. Plus a case (ALL CAPS vs Title) + leading-star study. Light + dark, 400dp, shown against a neighbouring non-recommended card.
decision: R1 (pill on its own line below the name) shipped in OnboardingScreen.EngineCard. Root cause was layout ordering: the pill shared the name Row's weight(1f) and a long name char-wrapped it vertically; its own line can't be crushed. Case left as the existing ALL-CAPS onboarding_recommended string (unchanged).

title: Languages Affordance Lab
summary: Make Kokoro's '9 languages' spec value read as tappable and give it a real (~44-48dp) touch target. Today it's icon-right with 2dp padding and reads as static text. 7 options: L1 icon-left roomy target (Max's steer), L2 underlined link, L3 chip/button, L4 chevron disclosure, L5 value + 'see all' hint, L6 two-letter code chips (Max what-if; collapses the two Englishes / mixes code systems), L7 '(i) See all 9 >' combined (L4 chevron is the fallback). Each shown in the real 118dp spec column with the tap-rect overlaid; dialog it opens shown for reference. Light + dark, 400dp.
decision: L7 ('(i) See all N >') shipped in EngineSpecColumn.EngineLanguagesValue: leading info glyph + 'See all 9' + trailing chevron, tinted colorScheme.primary (matches the app's other in-app link actions), full-width ~44dp touch target. New string engine_languages_see_all across all 8 locales; the now-orphaned engine_languages_count plural was removed. The 'LANGUAGES' overline supplies the noun the action drops. L4 (chevron only) remains the noted fallback if the double-glyph reads busy on device.

title: App Icon Lab
summary: Differentiate the TTS launcher icon from the marmalade agent app icon (identical jar + orange field). 9 mark variants x 5 background fields.
decision: Mark = V2, the jar with sound waves. (V5-e5, the speech-bubble jar, shipped first and was then superseded when V2 was revisited with a tuned background.) Composition, gradient and mascot finishing moved to icon-position-lab and icon-v2-lab.

title: Icon Composition Lab
summary: Jar size and corner position vs speech-bubble placement, under the circular launcher mask.
decision: Superseded — the speech-bubble mark (V5) lost to V2 sound waves, so its composition study no longer feeds the shipping icon. Kept for the finding it produced: the round mask cuts the top-right corner first, so growing the jar requires pulling the corner element inward.

title: V2 Sound-Waves Lab
summary: Final tuning of the shipping icon: wave centring, background gradient (geometry, ramp depth/spread/curve), and mascot finishing (sticker outline, drop shadow, gloss, eye treatments).
decision: SHIPPED 2026-08-01. Layout locked at X +4, Y 0, jar 0.78, waves 1.00, gap 5.5, arcs on the eye line, 3 arcs. Background: 45 degree linear, deep-amber ramp end, depth 0.56 / spread 0.62 / curve 1.00. Mascot: lid-cream sticker outline 2.4, drop shadow 0.18 at distance 1.6, body gloss 0.75, no sheen or rim, solid eye gloss at 1.0. Generated into the app by docs/design/build-launcher-icon.mjs.
